title: Two-function reverse hypercontractivity
statement: Let $p,q,\rho\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $p<1$, $q<1$, $0\le\rho\le1$, and $\rho^2\le(1-p)(1-q)$. For all nonnegative real-valued functions $f,g$ on the Boolean cube, their uniform inner product after applying the noise operator to $g$ satisfies $\langle f,T_\rho g\rangle\ge M_p(f)M_q(g)$.
hypotheses_covered: p, q, and ρ are real
f and g are real-valued functions on the Boolean cube
f is nonnegative at every cube point
g is nonnegative at every cube point
replaced: Let $p,q<1$, $0\le\rho\le1$, and $\rho^2\le(1-p)(1-q)$. For all $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to[0,\infty)$, uniform expectation satisfies $\E[fT_\rho g]\ge M_p(f)M_q(g)$. For nonnegative functions $u$, the extended mean is $M_r(u)=(\E u^r)^{1/r}$ when $r>0$; the same formula applies for $r<0$ when $u$ is positive everywhere. For positive $u$, $M_0(u)=\exp(\E\log u)$; if $r\le0$ and $u$ has a zero, $M_r(u)=0$. All expectations are uniform. For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform measure.
